prerequisites: Successful completion of modules to be completed in the 1st and 2nd semesters according to the study plan.

learning_outcomes.text: Students observe and reflect on competence development processes in themselves and in others. They analyze processes that lead to the building and development of competence. They describe competence as a construct based on different development theories. They analyze factors that influence individual and cooperative competence development. Development processes are described using diagnostic instruments.

Students experience their individual and cooperative competence development as a malleable and controllable process. Tools for self-management are taught and applied using learning strategies and scientific working techniques. Both strategies for primary process design and independent regulation and control are used.

The competence acquired so far is systematically reflected upon using concepts/models and theories, areas with development needs are identified, instruments and strategies for one's own development are applied, and concepts for designing development concepts are created.

The systematic engagement with one's own development process as well as with concepts and models from theory introduces students to the scientific attitude of research-based learning. Through comparison, students should be able to take on more responsibility for their own development processes.
Individual control and design of one's own competence acquisition
Design of processes in work teams
Integration of media as tools for competence development

Students acquire the ability to explore the complexity of the school field from a professional and system-oriented perspective and to perceive and reflect on practice and learning fields related to school.
Students acquire the ability to establish initial relationships between educational science/vocational pedagogical theoretical approaches and concrete pedagogical situations.

Students acquire the ability to try out initial pedagogical action possibilities, especially those aimed at acquiring professional action competence, and to reflect on study and career choices against the background of the experience gained.
Students acquire the ability to reflectively shape the structure and design of their studies and their own professional development.
Students gain an overview of the development of didactic theories, models and concepts.
Students know didactic models, their theoretical considerations and basic positions.
Students can follow the historical development process in didactic thinking.
Students are able to plan and justify their own didactic actions on the basis of the acquired knowledge.

syllabus_topics: Overview of learning, competence, and learning theory
Structures of education and their relation to competence development
Designing learning processes considering heterogeneity and individualization
Development in didactic thinking of vocational education
Relevance of historical models for current didactic thinking

assessment_methods.method: Presentation (approx. 30 minutes) with written elaboration (approx. 10 pages) or oral exam (approx. 30 minutes)

assessment_rules: The module is passed if the module partial examinations are passed. The module is weighted with its number of credit points (factor: 1).
